rules_primary: If Graham Platner drops out of the 2026 United States Senate election in Maine before Jul 13, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
“Dropped out” means any of the following:
Graham Platner announces they are ending, suspending, or withdrawing from their campaign
Graham Platner files official withdrawal paperwork with relevant election authorities
Graham Platner publicly states they are no longer seeking the office
Graham Platner endorses another candidate while stating they are no longer running
Graham Platner is disqualified by election authorities or courts and does not appeal

The following do NOT constitute dropping out:
Losing a primary or election
Failing to qualify for debates or ballots
Temporarily suspending campaign activities without withdrawing
Being eliminated through the normal election process
Reducing campaign activities while remaining a candidate

Key provisions:
Once someone drops out per above criteria, the market resolves YES even if they later re-enter
“Suspending” a campaign is treated as dropping out unless Graham Platner explicitly states they remain a candidate
For primary races, dropping out of the presidential race entirely counts as dropping out of that party’s primary
Withdrawing from the race counts even if the person remains on the ballot

rules_primary: If Graham Platner drops out of the 2026 United States Senate election in Maine before Jul 12, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
“Dropped out” means any of the following:
Graham Platner announces they are ending, suspending, or withdrawing from their campaign
Graham Platner files official withdrawal paperwork with relevant election authorities
Graham Platner publicly states they are no longer seeking the office
Graham Platner endorses another candidate while stating they are no longer running
Graham Platner is disqualified by election authorities or courts and does not appeal

The following do NOT constitute dropping out:
Losing a primary or election
Failing to qualify for debates or ballots
Temporarily suspending campaign activities without withdrawing
Being eliminated through the normal election process
Reducing campaign activities while remaining a candidate

Key provisions:
Once someone drops out per above criteria, the market resolves YES even if they later re-enter
“Suspending” a campaign is treated as dropping out unless Graham Platner explicitly states they remain a candidate
For primary races, dropping out of the presidential race entirely counts as dropping out of that party’s primary
Withdrawing from the race counts even if the person remains on the ballot
